title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
Deepfake pornography depicting real women without their consent was created and distributed on an online platform. The victims included entertainers, television presenters, athletes, government officials, and members of the royal family. The system that enabled this deployment was an image or video generation tool connected to a platform with millions of users, operating without the human review needed to prevent non-consensual sexual imagery from being created and hosted.

This is a failure of both the technology provider and the hosting platform. The generation tool did not refuse requests to create sexual deepfakes of identifiable people. The platform did not detect or remove such content at scale. Neither system had controls sufficient to prevent this class of harm, despite the legal status of non-consensual sexual imagery being established in the jurisdictions involved.

It is not established whether the platform knew what content it was hosting before victims reported it, or what remediation it undertook after the reports became public.

summary:
Multiple prominent Dutch women are considering filing charges after appearing in manipulated pornographic videos on an online platform that receives 13 million monthly visitors. The platform contains fake videos featuring Dutch entertainers, television presenters, Olympic athletes, government officials, and members of the royal family. Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos disgusting and urged victims to report them. Managers and representatives of various victims confirmed to NOS that they have filed reports or are considering legal action. The names of victims are being withheld to protect their privacy.

Deepfake pornography falls under revenge porn laws and is therefore criminal. An attorney warned that without government intervention, more fake videos will emerge. Victims have several options including filing reports with the public prosecutor, starting a class action lawsuit, filing complaints with the data protection authority, or contacting hosting companies. Previously, television presenter Welmoed Sijtsma was victimized by such videos and created a documentary about her experience. A 39-year-old man from Amersfoort was convicted last November and received a conditional sentence of 180 hours for making her fake videos.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
